releases.notes:
## [0.5.2] — 2026-10-23

### Added

- Add built-in chunk-map warnings for failed and partially saved exports, with
  purple conflict hints and simplified markers in small cells. Show all export
  states, terrain/entity results, and metadata status in hover details; keep
  Xaero and in-world overlays free of corner glyphs.
- Surface automatic/manual export and file-operation failures through merged,
  rate-limited chat and toast notices, with current health on the status screen.

### Changed

- Reduce entity snapshot copying and index reconciliation by chunk, keeping
  small observations fast even after a long capture session.
- Share spatial queries and bucket summaries across chunk maps and world
  overlays; publish changed export-state regions and bound coarse-view refresh
  work with large capture histories.
- Replace the vendored NBT stack with bounded native codecs and read-only MCA
  access; stream entity rewrites and apply conflicts in bounded batches.
- Keep routing previews off disk-write locks and skip unchanged folder claims.

### Fixed

- Detect obsolete mirror generators despite current metadata and offer backed-up
  repair; preserve valid customizations and refuse unknown generator edits.
- Preserve captured terrain, lighting, entities, and inventories across source
  changes and concurrent exports. Resume interrupted capture scans and retain
  confirmed block removals under queue pressure.
- Retry only unfinished mirror data, including after disconnecting. Preserve
  each source's terrain/entity order while letting newer terrain proceed past
  entity-only failures.
- Protect open saves with Minecraft's session lock across Windows and Linux.
  Preserve damaged region headers and healthy neighboring durability claims.
  Recover interrupted file sets without overwriting unknown edits or undoing
  verified commits after cleanup failures; retain legacy timestamps when migration
  or metadata persistence fails.
- Preserve damaged configuration and optional saved data, defer overwrites when
  priority rules are unreadable, and keep independent terrain saves running.
- Validate mirror identities and relocation plans before moving files; recover
  routing consistently and reject stale mapping updates.
- Resolve conflicts without lock-order deadlocks, support external chunk files,
  and retain failed or newer incoming conflicts for review.
- Correct entity moves, detached passengers, and observations that revert during
  an export. Preserve legacy UUID trees missing type IDs while rejecting malformed
  new entity observations and oversized NBT strings.
- Preserve container names and inventories without applying stale data across
  worlds or block-entity types, or restoring block entities into confirmed air.
- Refresh map aggregation after panning and bound work for extreme viewports.
- Handle unsafe folder names and custom dimension paths; preserve nearby-export
  entities, Unicode names, spawn dimensions, and independent lineage.
- Finish accepted exports and one final queued pass on exit without interrupting
  atomic writes or keeping an idle export worker alive.

### Known Issues

- The in-world overlay does not work when shaders are enabled.

releases.notes:
## [0.5.1] — 2026-10-18

### Added

- Added Session and Map color modes for the in-world overlay. Session keeps its
  yellow/green/blue coverage palette; Map shares the built-in and Xaero maps'
  capture-age, source, and live queue colors, including coarse aggregation.

### Changed

- Raised the default fixed in-world overlay height to 96. Existing configured
  heights are preserved.

### Fixed

- Include replay imports as historical blue coverage in Session mode, regardless
  of their timestamps, and retain historical cached coverage between sessions.

### Known Issues

- The in-world overlay does not work when shaders are enabled.

releases.notes:
## [0.5.0] — 2026-10-18

### Added

- Added an in-world chunk overlay showing queued captures, chunks captured in
  the current session, and previously saved chunks. Source worlds and mirror
  worlds have independent visibility settings; **K** toggles the setting for
  the current world type. Thanks to [@cev-api](https://github.com/cev-api) for
  the original [PR #14](https://github.com/billstark001/world-mirror/pull/14).

### Changed

- Prepared lightweight overlay state before drawing, reused the map's indexed
  snapshots and bounded bucket sizing, and merged adjacent same-colour tiles.
  The default overlay radius is 128 chunks; larger views use coarse tiles.
- Fixed degenerate faces in the chunk-box geometry and prevented distant
  outlines from fading to the sky's fog colour. Kept the PR's Gradle cache-path
  change separate from this release.
- Restored visible grid lines in both directions, with a switch for same-status
  interior boundaries, and reduced the default fill and outline opacity to 60%
  of its previous strength. Removed translucent internal side faces that left
  one-directional stripes even when the grid was hidden.
- Kept the optional Xaero bridge off the development client's runtime classpath,
  so World Mirror can launch without Xaero's World Map installed.
- Kept the custom Cloth Config select for enums. Boolean and short bounded
  integer fields can opt into it explicitly; current fields use their default
  controls. The 8–16384 chunk overlay radius uses a bounded text field for
  exact values.
- Stopped in-world overlay extraction when it is hidden, including under F1
  by default. A separate setting can keep it visible under F1.

### Fixed

- Added opt-in development Xaero bridge runtime dependencies with
  `-PxaeroIntegration=true`, while keeping startup without Xaero supported.
- Render the in-world overlay after water, clouds, and transparency composition
  on the classic path, with the grid drawn after the fill. Minecraft 26.3 retains
  native improved-transparency rendering.
- Keep chunk boxes while blending only their camera-facing shell, avoiding doubled
  opacity from front and back faces.

releases.notes:
## [0.4.6] — 2026-10-05

### Added

- Show live cached chunks and capture/write queues on the built-in map and Xaero
  World Map overlay. Four yellow-to-green colours distinguish pending captures
  and pending writes with or without an existing saved record.
- Show separate saved, memory-cached, and pending-write chunk counts on the
  status screen.

### Changed

- Colour toolkit replay imports with the same capture-age gradient as World
  Mirror chunks, while retaining their source in the map tooltip.
- Record new successful sync times using chunk capture timestamps. Existing
  metadata timestamps are not migrated.

### Fixed

- Keep chunk-status snapshots consistent across concurrent refreshes and
  invalidations, and avoid scanning empty map regions or all saved boundaries
  on every frame.
- Guard Xaero overlay rendering against invalid projections and extreme zoom.

## world-mirror-format [0.1.1] — 2026-09-27

### Changed

- Published the binary and source JARs as direct GitHub Release assets so Gradle
  consumers can resolve the version through a public Ivy repository without a
  neighboring source checkout or Maven Central.
